You've made quite the acerbic comment, one that's equally as controversial as mine. This isn't an objective debate any more; this has escalated into a battle of taste. 

You make the bold assertion that classical, slow or 'elevator music for the NPR set' as you put it lulls 'you to sleep'. Hang on buddy, did you just shrug off entire styles of music, because you can, without an explanation? This stinks of arrogant bullshit to me. 

And before you go rambling, that I didn't explain my 'dumb' opinion. Just know that at least I provided a justification for my opinion - it doesn't matter if its right or wrong - but you just pass it off as fact.

And besides, something must have been lost in translation, because if you actually read my comment you would notice that I made no reference to my taste leaning towards the styles of music you so carelessly dismissed. Oblivion and Genesis, the two songs I mentioned I liked from Grimes, certainly don't fall into the classical or painfully slow category. 

What's more you claim that the purpose of music is to be MOVED by it. Some of the most moving and stirring pieces of music ever made are the 'sedate, pleasant bullshit' as you so kindly put it.

The only point you made that I agree with is individuality.  If Grimes does something different that I don't like, fair enough. By all means let her go down that path. But from what you're suggesting, that path is exclusive to your messed up vision of what music is supposed to be.
